latest_final: Kameda was the reigning monarch, and Umio was a non-royal challenger for political control of the same kingdom. Kameda defeated Umio. After their deaths, Kameda was cremated, a more honorific treatment, while Umio was buried intact in a deliberately less prestigious burial arranged by Kameda’s side. People comparing their funerals took that contrast as evidence that Umio had lost. Kameda’s fragments resulted from cremation, not from damage Umio inflicted during their struggle.
